ghi_chu.mo_ta: Narrow-framed vertical sash windows with thin glazing bars and many small panes, in the brick houses at the left. They sit beside the leaded diamond-pane casements.
ghi_chu.ly_do: Sash windows were only just appearing in England around 1670–1690. Slim, regular multi-pane sashes in an ordinary street look more like the Georgian period than 1680.

ghi_chu.mo_ta: A dark, thin vertical downpipe runs down the brick facade at the left, next to the eaves gutter.
ghi_chu.ly_do: This looks like a uniform, cast-iron-style rainwater pipe. Such pipes were uncommon before the 18th century, and 1680 houses mostly had lead or no downpipes.
